positions.as_written: Learn the femoral point as a set of offsets, as on the medial side.
Count the holes in the patella across all operations a patient has had, since each one reduces the bone's strength.
Consider patellar vascularity before combining a lateral release with anterior or distal surgery.
Protect the infrapatellar branch, and warn the patient about numbness in advance rather than afterwards.
Treat femoral accuracy as the single most consequential variable.
Plan the whole construct before starting, since proximal and distal procedures interact through the extensor vector.
Assess previous surgery for holes in the patella and for lateral release, and weigh the vascular cost before adding to either.
Avoid combining a lateral release with distal realignment without a reason, because the patella's supply is the thing being spent.
Plan from those, and 7.57 carries the rest.
